quotes.text: With Compute Fleet, you list multiple acceptable VM sizes. Azure can then place some workers on one size and others on another as long as your workload runs on both.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains the core idea of the service: flexibility across VM sizes instead of one exact SKU.

quotes.text: A Spot VM is not the place for the only copy of an important database, a single user facing server, or a job that loses hours of progress when one worker stops.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clear guidance on which workloads do not belong on evictable capacity.

quotes.text: If you're scaling an application because user traffic changes, start with virtual machine scale sets. If you're gathering a large amount of flexible compute because a job needs many workers, look at compute fleet.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A compact decision rule between two related Azure services.

quotes.text: Here's the mistake most people make. They treat compute fleet as automatic application recovery. It does not do that. It manages capacity. Your job system still needs to recover the work.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Names a common misconception and the shared-responsibility boundary.

takeaways: Azure Compute Fleet lets you request a large pool of capacity across several acceptable VM sizes, zones and pricing models instead of betting a deployment on one exact SKU.
Mixing on-demand VMs as a stable baseline with Spot VMs for extra throughput only works when progress lives outside the worker, in durable queues, checkpoints and retry-safe tasks.
Virtual machine scale sets fit steady application tiers that serve user traffic, while Compute Fleet fits batch, simulation, rendering and other work that splits across many independent workers.
hook: Large batch jobs often stall because one exact VM size has no capacity when it is needed. This episode is for Azure architects and platform teams running simulations, rendering, testing or data processing at scale. You learn how Azure Compute Fleet, Spot VMs and a retry-safe workload design keep big jobs moving at a controlled cost.
